title: Environment file: dev, staging, prod
description: One file for each environment, named after it (prod.yaml). Pillars and systems are shared by every environment; this file says what differs.

fallbackMetric.description: Another metric to read in place of the one it belongs to, when that gives no number or 0 (the autoscale ceiling, then the fixed throughput of an account without autoscale). It has no over or orElse of its own.

metricSignal.description: Where one signal's number comes from. The town reads fractions (0.42 is 42%) and rates per second.

metric.description: The metric's name as the cloud spells it.

aggregation.description: How the points of the window are added up. Default average.

filter.description: A dimension filter, for example StatusCode eq '429'.

scale.description: Multiplies the value. A percentage has scale 0.01. Default 1.

perSecond.description: Divide by the seconds of the window, to turn a total into a rate.

over.description: Another metric the value is divided by (provisioned capacity, all requests), which gives a share. It may have an orElse of its own.

name.description: Name in the environment picker. Defaults to the file name.

order.description: Where it stands in the picker, lowest first. Ties go by id.

default.description: The environment shown when none is asked for. Without one, the first.

sources.description: Where this environment's numbers come from, by source name. The names metrics and messaging are what the signals use unless a signal says otherwise (see signals); incidents is where open incidents come from. Any other kebab-case name defines a source a signal can be pointed at.

kind.description: The kind of source. Which kinds exist depends on the adapters loaded (the adapters folder beside the program): fake and prometheus are built in, the Azure ones come with the azure adapter. `validate` checks the kind against them. A kind accepted before the adapter that reads it exists shows no data.

connection.description: How to reach it (a workspace, an endpoint). Not used by the fake source.

credential.description: Sources that sign in only: the login to use, by name from credentials. Without it, the one called default, else the kind's usual login (the Azure CLI, az login, for Azure sources).

pollSeconds.description: How often the source is asked. Default 30.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long one ask may take before it is given up. Default 10.

query.description: Sources that send a query (loganalytics): the query, a template. {window} and {windowSeconds} stand for the window, {roles} for the telemetry names of the systems asked about (double-quoted, comma separated); scope variables and {environment} work too. It returns one row per telemetry name with the columns role, calls, errors and latencyMs.

regionQuery.description: Request sources (loganalytics): the query that says how each service's requests divide between regions, a template like query. It returns one row per telemetry name and region with the columns role, region and calls. Sampled counts are fine: only the proportions are used. Without it the split is not measured.

window.description: Query sources: how far back one answer looks, a number and a unit (30s, 5m, 1h). Default 5m. A system with fewer calls than its minCalls in this window is quiet. Platform-metric sources (azuremonitor) look back this far too.

metrics.description: Platform-metric sources (azuremonitor): which metric of which resources fills which signal. The program knows no metric name; everything is written here. Each entry takes the resources one rule of scope.resources finds for a system; a system's value is the worst (highest) over its resources.

resources.description: The name of a scope.resources rule.

namespace.description: The metric namespace, for a resource type that has more than one. Usually left out.

interval.description: The time grain the metrics are asked at. Default 1m. Some metrics do not support a minute (Cosmos provisioned throughput needs 5m or more); then give the entry a longer interval and a window that holds a few points of it.

window.description: How far back this entry looks, a number and a unit (15m, 1h). Without it the source's window applies. It must hold at least two points of the entry's interval.

credentials.description: How sources sign in, by name. A source without a credential uses the one called default, else its kind's usual login; to change that for all of them, define one called default.

kind.description: The way to sign in; the adapters loaded say which exist. The azure adapter has azure-cli (whoever az login signed in), default (the Azure SDK's usual chain), managed-identity (the identity of the machine it runs on) and service-principal (an app registration).

tenantId.description: The directory to sign in to. Without it, the login's own.

clientId.description: The app registration (service-principal) or user-assigned identity (managed-identity).

clientSecretEnv.description: service-principal only: the name of the environment variable that holds the secret. The secret itself never goes in a registry file.

signals.description: Which source each signal comes from in this environment: a source name from sources, or none. A signal not listed here uses the source called metrics (messaging for backlog and deadLetters). A signal with no source is absent: not shown, not grey.

tenants.description: The tenants of this environment. Each has a database in every system with a tenantPattern.

id.description: Goes into the database name where the tenantPattern has {tenant}.

name.description: What the tenant is called on screen.

kind.description: A test tenant (smoke tests, QA, sandboxes) is drawn paler and striped, can be hidden, and shows amber at worst, never red.

logs.description: What a system's Logs tab shows in a live town: 5xx requests, slow requests, warnings and errors, and exceptions, as four separate sections. Nothing is polled; the query runs only when the tab is opened and its answer is not kept. Without this block the tab says logs are not set up.

source.description: The loganalytics source (from sources) whose workspace and login are used.

query.description: The query, a template. {roles} stands for the system's telemetry name (double-quoted), {from} and {to} for the UTC bounds (ISO 8601), {window}, {windowSeconds}, {slaMs} (the system's p99 SLA) and {kind} (api, worker and so on); scope variables and {environment} work too. It returns one row for each kind of entry with the columns section (failed, slow, logs or exceptions), at and text; count, level, durationMs and result may be left out.

window.description: How far back it looks. Default 4h.

links.description: Links in the header of a section of the Logs tab that open the telemetry store's own search, already filtered to the system, 0 to n. Each resource the named assets rule finds gets its own link.

name.description: The words on the link, for example 5xx in App Insights. When the rule finds more than one resource, the resource's name is added.

section.description: The section whose header carries the link.

resources.description: The name of a scope.assets rule. Each resource it finds gets its own link.

url.description: A template that starts with https:// (or http://) written out. Holes: {resourceId}, {resourceIdTwice} (percent-encoded twice, for a portal that nests the id in its own address), {resourceName}, {role}, {from}, {to}, {windowMs}, {environment} and your variables. Values are percent-encoded.

links.description: Finds the calls the systems really make from the dependency data in the telemetry and adds them to the declared calls and gatewayCalls. Without this block the environment has only the declared links. Found links are saved under _discovered/links/<environment>/ in the town's folder, never in a pillar file.

source.description: The loganalytics source (from sources) whose workspace and login are used.

query.description: The query, a template. {roles} stands for the telemetry names of the systems asked about (double-quoted, comma separated), {from} and {to} for the read's UTC bounds (ISO 8601); scope variables and {environment} work too. It returns one row for each caller and address with the columns caller, host and days (an array of the days it was seen on); path and calls may be left out.

firstRead.description: How far back the first read looks, and the longest gap a later read covers. Default 7d.

minDays.description: The fewest different days a call must be seen on to be drawn. Default 2.

keepFor.description: How long a link stays after it was last seen. Default 30d.

ignoreHosts.description: Regular expressions for addresses that are platform noise.

rules.description: The ways an address becomes a system, tried in order.

host.description: A regular expression over the host, with named groups (?<name>...).

path.description: A regular expression over the path, with named groups, for a gateway that names the destination in it.

target.description: The system id, with {name} holes for the named groups and {callerPillar} for the pillar of the caller.

gateway.description: The call goes through the API gateway.

aliases.description: Words the address uses that the registry spells differently, applied to every captured group.

traffic.description: Measures how much each town system sends to each API, so the traffic no town system explains (the outside traffic, drawn at the airport) can be told from the rest: outside = the API's measured total minus what its town callers send. Without it the split is not measured.

query.description: A template like links.query, read over the share window. It returns one row for each caller and address with the columns caller, host and calls (the estimated calls, corrected for sampling); path for a gateway.

shareWindow.description: How far back each read looks, which smooths the shares. Default 1h.

minCalls.description: Below this many observed calls to an API the share is too noisy: the last good one stands, marked estimated. Default 20.

scope.description: How this environment's pillars and systems map onto the cloud: the subscription of each pillar, the workspace, which resources belong to a service and what the telemetry calls each system. Every convention is a rule or a template here; the program assumes none. Templates have {variable} and {variable|filter} holes (filters: nospace, lower, upper); {environment} is this file's id and variables are your own.

inventory.description: The source (from sources) that reads the inventory, a resourcegraph source. Without it, the only one.

workspace.description: The workspace the telemetry is in, by name or wildcard pattern (for example log-*-{env}), a template over {environment} and variables. A name is looked up in the inventory (through Resource Graph) and exactly one workspace must match. An id or resource id written here is used as it is.

workspaceId.description: The workspace's id (a GUID, or a resource id), a template. When it is given it is used as it is and the name is not looked up.

variables.description: Your own words for the templates, for example env: prd.

subscription.description: How a pillar finds its subscription: by name or by tag (exactly one). Templates over {pillar} (its scope.code, else its id), {pillarId}, {environment} and variables.

nameLike.description: A wildcard (* and ?) matched, ignoring case, against the subscriptions' names, for example *-{env}-{pillar}.

pillars.description: Pillars named instead of found: pillar id to subscription id.

resources.description: Which resources belong to a service.

name.description: Names the rule in what the inspector shows.

types.description: The resource types it applies to, for example microsoft.web/serverfarms.

pattern.description: A regular expression over the resource's name, ignoring case. Named groups: service (required) is matched with a system's serviceCode; role (api, worker...), pillar, region and tenant are optional.

roles.description: Only systems of these roles. Without it, all.

serviceTag.description: A tag that names the service, for a resource whose name does not match the pattern.

tenantNameTag.description: The tag that holds a tenant's friendly name, on resources whose pattern has a tenant group.

instances.description: A query expression that counts the instances one resource runs (for example a plan's workers). A system's instances are the sum over its resources of rules that have one.

state.description: A query expression that reads one resource's app state as text. A system whose rule has it shows Running, Stopped (a building under construction) or, when the inventory has no such app, Missing (grey, not found).

running.description: The values of state that mean the app runs; any other value is shown as stopped. Required with state.

cloud.description: What the cloud is called in your words, for example Azure. A system whose app the inventory cannot find reads not found in <cloud>; without it, not found in the inventory.

assets.description: Resources that are not systems but stand in the town as small buildings without health, such as a key vault or a storage account. They are looked for in each pillar's subscription. One that names a service stands beside that service's pad; the rest stand in the pillar's back yard. The drawer shows its name, what it is, the service it belongs to and its portal links.

label.description: What the resource is, in the words of the drawer, for example Key vault.

shape.description: How the building looks. Default box.

types.description: The resource types it applies to.

pattern.description: A regular expression over the resource's name, ignoring case. Optional named groups: service (matched with a system's serviceCode), pillar (another pillar's resource is left out) and region.

telemetryRole.description: What the telemetry calls a system that has no telemetry.role of its own: a template over {system}, {service}, {name}, {role}, {pillar}, {pillarId}, {environment} and variables.

links.description: Addresses that open a resource somewhere else, such as its page in a cloud portal or console. They show next to each resource in the inspector's Config tab. The program only shows them as links (it never calls them) and holds no credentials for them. Without links, none is shown.

name.description: The words on the link, for example Cloud portal.

url.description: A template that starts with https:// (or http://) written out. Holes: {resourceId}, {name}, {type}, {region}, {subscriptionId}, {tenantId}, {tenantName}, {environment} and your variables. Values are percent-encoded; a resource id keeps its slashes.

types.description: Only resources of these types. Without it, every resource.

regions.description: How a service's region is read and named, and when a lopsided split of requests is flagged. A service shows it only when its resources are in two or more regions.

tag.description: The tag of a resource that says its region. Without it, the region group of the rule's pattern, else the location the cloud gives.

names.description: Region value to the label shown (for example northeurope: North). A value without a label is shown as it is.

skew.description: The share of a service's requests one region may take while another region runs instances, before the town flags it. Default 0.9; 1 never flags.

queries.description: Replaces the inventory source's own queries. {types} in resources stands for the quoted resource types the rules name.

workspaces.description: Returns id, name and customerId (the workspace id) of every workspace; the name is matched against scope.workspace.

exclude.description: Systems that are not deployed in this environment. They are left out of its town, and an island with no system left is not on the map.

fake.description: Settings for the fake source only.

undeclaredTenants.description: Tenants the fake source finds in the data that the tenants list does not name, so the town can show an unknown tenant.
